newsitem.title: USA: Boston Life's Troponin slows breast cancer.
newsitem.headline: Boston Life's Troponin slows breast cancer.

text.p: Boston Life Sciences Inc said on Monday that Troponin I significantly inhibited the growth of experimental primary human breast cancer in mice.

The company said that when it implanted human breast cancer into nude mice and then administered recombinant Troponin I subcutaneously over a 28-day period, tumor growth in the treated animals was significantly inhibited compared with tumor growth in the control mice.
Troponin I is an anti-angiogenic product in preclinical development. Angiogenesis is the formation and differentiation of blood vessels.

"The results of this study, together with our previously reported results showing inhibition of human prostate cancer growth in mice by Troponin, provide further important evidence of the potential therapeutic efficacy of this naturally-derived anti-angiogenic protein for the treatment of a variety of clinically important solid tumors," said Marc Lanser, Chief Scientific Officer of Boston Life.
Boston Life is engaged in the research and development of novel treatments for cancer, autoimmune diseases and central nervous system disorders.
